sections.heading: Neutral-point voltage oscillation
sections.text: Same as NPC: reduce balancing loop gain or increase DC-bus capacitance. The T-type bidirectional switches carry more current during zero-level, so thermal stress can cause asymmetric behavior if the switches are overheating.

sections.heading: THD failure
sections.text: Same as NPC: check LCL filter resonance, active damping, dead-time compensation. T-type has slightly different harmonic distortion pattern because the zero-level path has different impedance than NPC.

sections.heading: Overshoot from voltage loop
sections.text: Same as NPC: reduce voltage-loop kp or fix anti-windup. The voltage-loop design is identical to NPC — the three-level structure does not change the voltage-loop dynamics.

sections.heading: Efficiency below spec
sections.text: T-type efficiency is dominated by the bidirectional switch conduction losses during zero-level. At high DC-bus voltage (>600V), the bidirectional switches must be higher-voltage-rated with higher conduction loss. Consider switching to NPC topology.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the T-type cannot meet specs at the required voltage level, consider NPC (better at >600V) or two-level with higher switching frequency (simpler but higher THD). For very high voltage, cascaded H-bridge is the standard choice.
